g.title: Case and channel [observed]
g.desc: Corrected event CSV: CaseId, Activity, Actor; order channel comes from the source file. No customer identity or timestamp is available. Sales IDs are not case IDs.

g.title: Pizza type / size [source fields]
g.desc: The Sales worksheets record Pizza Type and Pizza Size. Using those fields as a preparation specification is an authored information-flow assumption; there is no row-level sales-to-case join.

g.title: Price catalogue [source]
g.desc: PizzasInfo: 18 type/size entries, recorded cost and revenue. Monetary unit is unspecified. The association with settlement describes a proposed information interface, not a recorded data exchange.

g.title: Recorded sales [source]
g.desc: Sales fields: Id, StructureId, Pizza Type, Pizza Size, Revenue, Cost, Satisfaction, Weekday, Customer Location, Customer Type. This is a sales record, not proof of a distinct customer or an event-log transaction. Cached Excel values are used; formulas are never executed.

g.title: Customer location [source field]
g.desc: Customer Location is a geographic category in Sales, not a street address or a case-linked delivery instruction. Its proposed use in planning is an explicit modeling assumption.

g.title: Loops and order flexibility are observed; their business cause and timing are unknown.
g.desc: Prepare -> Bake -> Pack repeats one to three times in the logs. The model generalizes this as a loop; no defect/rework cause or one-cycle/one-sale equivalence is asserted. Cash and Give order occur in both orders. Logical parallel routing expresses that flexibility, not simultaneous human work. Branch labels are explanatory, not an executable decision engine.
